entries.core_move: Characterize the unit impulse by using its zero-width, unit-area behavior to treat $\delta$(t) as the impulse building block for continuous-time signal descriptions.
Distinguish impulse area from ordinary signal amplitude when interpreting unit impulse terms in continuous-time signal constructions.
Interpret the coefficient in a scaled impulse as the impulse area that weights $\delta$(t) in continuous-time signal expressions.
Locate a shifted impulse by reading the time value that makes its argument zero and carrying its area weight in continuous-time impulse expressions.

entries.lesson_title: Multiplying a Function by an Impulse
entries.core_move: Reduce a product $f(t)$$\delta$(t) to $f(0)$$\delta$(t) by recognizing that the impulse keeps only the function value at $t = 0$.

entries.lesson_title: Multiplying a Function by a Shifted Impulse
entries.core_move: Convert $f(t)$$\delta$(t - t0) into $f(t0)$$\delta$(t - t0) by evaluating the function at the shifted impulse location.
